teaser.en: A buttressed forest tree with smooth dark bark whose reddish fruits are worth the walk when ripe.

summary.en: *Mwawa* is an evergreen tree of the coastal forest, standing on a buttressed base with smooth, dark bark. Its reddish fruit is eaten when ripe.

about.en: *Mwawa* is an evergreen tree whose trunk flares into buttresses at the base. The bark is smooth and dark. It belongs to the cocoa-plum family, and it bears small reddish fruits.

uses.en: The ripe fruit is edible and eaten as a wild snack.

names.en: The Digo name *mwawa* is recorded in ICRAF's handbook of useful trees, where it appears under a different but related tree, the mobola plum (*Parinari curatellifolia*). The two may share the name, or one may be a mix-up. No Swahili or English common name has been recorded for *Hirtella zanzibarica*.
